summary.text: James P. Lappe is the Democratic candidate for the Missouri House of Representatives, District 81, in the November 3, 2026 general election, after winning the August 4 Democratic primary for the open seat.

A former St. Louis alderman who works for the Missouri AFL-CIO, he said in a Ballotpedia survey that his priorities include defending the initiative petition process, addressing affordability, and protecting workers' rights.

paragraphs.text: James P. Lappe was born in Creve Coeur, Missouri, and Ballotpedia lists a bachelor's degree from the University of Missouri-St. Louis (2007) and a graduate degree from the University of Missouri-Kansas City (2013).
In a Ballotpedia survey, he said he grew up in the St. Louis area and moved to the city after completing his master's degree in 2013.
He said he worked for Missouri Jobs with Justice from 2017 to 2023 and now coordinates the Dislocated Worker Program at the Missouri AFL-CIO.
Lappe served on the St. Louis Board of Aldermen for the 11th Ward from 2022 to 2023, finishing the unexpired term of Sarah Wood Martin.

He said that as an alderman he helped pass board bills that modernized the city's plumbing code, gave workers a voice in the governance of the firefighters' pension system, and established a Reproductive Equity Fund under the city Health Department.
In the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary for District 81, he defeated Tony Kirchner and Aaron Clite with 46.6 percent of the vote.
Lappe said in the survey that he is a member of IBEW Local 1, has been a union member since 1999, and lives in Carondelet with his wife and daughter.
He listed his key messages as defending democracy and the initiative petition process, addressing Missouri's affordability crisis, and restoring local control for St. Louis and other jurisdictions.
